St Louis County Circuit Court: A Guide to Understanding the Judicial System in St Louis County

The St Louis County Circuit Court is one of the busiest judicial systems in Missouri. It is responsible for the administration of justice in the county, including civil and criminal cases, as well as juvenile, probate, and small claims cases. This article will provide an overview of the St Louis County Circuit Court, its structure, functions, and procedures.

Overview of the St Louis County Circuit Court

The St Louis County Circuit Court is part of the Missouri state court system and is located in Clayton, Missouri. It serves the entire St Louis County, which has a population of over one million people. The Circuit Court is the trial court of general jurisdiction, which means it has the authority to hear all types of cases, including civil, criminal, juvenile, probate, and small claims cases.

Structure of the St Louis County Circuit Court

The St Louis County Circuit Court has three main divisions: Civil, Criminal, and Family Court. Each division has several judges who are responsible for hearing cases and making decisions based on the law and evidence presented.

Civil Division

The Civil Division handles cases that involve disputes between two parties, such as personal injury, contract disputes, and property disputes. The Civil Division has several judges who are assigned to specific types of cases based on their expertise.

Criminal Division

The Criminal Division handles cases involving criminal offenses, such as theft, assault, and drug offenses. The Criminal Division also has several judges who are assigned to specific types of cases based on their expertise.

Family Court Division

The Family Court Division handles cases involving family-related issues, such as divorce, child custody, and child support. The Family Court Division also has several judges who are assigned to specific types of cases based on their expertise.

Procedures of the St Louis County Circuit Court

The procedures of the St Louis County Circuit Court vary depending on the type of case being heard. However, all cases in the Circuit Court follow a similar process.

Filing a Case

To file a case in the St Louis County Circuit Court, a person must complete the appropriate forms and pay a filing fee. The forms can be obtained online or in person at the Circuit Court Clerk's Office.

Pretrial Procedures

After a case is filed, the parties involved will go through a series of pretrial procedures, such as discovery, where each party gathers information about the case. They may also participate in mediation or other alternative dispute resolution methods to try to settle the case before trial.

Trial

If the case is not settled through alternative dispute resolution, it will proceed to trial. The trial is presided over by a judge, who will hear evidence from both parties and make a decision based on the law and evidence presented.

Appeals

If a party disagrees with the judge's decision, they may file an appeal with the Missouri Court of Appeals. The appeals court will review the case and either uphold or overturn the lower court's decision.
